items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name — she had to ask 'what is your name again?' at the end of a 13-minute call, and Frank never asked hers in return. Zero name uses on the whole call.
No 'How are you today?' and no rapport moment for a repeat customer — 'Oh, no kidding' was the entire acknowledgment that Einstein already moved her from Marshall to Georgetown last year.
Agenda statement had the roadmap and the ~10-minute timeframe but no confirmation ask — no 'Sound good?', so the agenda opener does not count.
No 'Pricing is super simple' framing before the numbers.

Never said what's included — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools. Then pitched a pad deposit without ever establishing that pads come standard, which risks reading as an upsell on something free.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no transportation fees.
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned on a move with two pianos going into long-term storage. Highest-value omission on the call.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.
No insurance explanation at all — neither No Worries nor the 60¢/lb baseline, on a two-piano job.

Packing service never offered or priced, even after she said 'I'm hoping to get all of the boxes done but we'll see' — Einstein packed ~75 boxes for her last time, so this was a live revenue door left shut.
Two pianos confirmed but never discussed — no specialty handling, no extra time, no specialty pricing, no reassurance.
Assembly/disassembly never addressed despite beds, mattresses and pianos.
Clock mechanics half-covered: gave the 2.5-hour minimum but never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never explained 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum.
No sense-check anywhere — the customer read the $1,300 / $3,500 numbers back to herself unprompted rather than Frank asking 'does that make sense?'
Save Your Ass prep speech completely absent on the single most applicable call type for it — a self-packing customer paying $400/hour.
No booking attempt. He confirmed Sept 11 availability in the first minute and never came back to ask for it; she left to 'compare quotes.'
'No deposit required' never mentioned — and the only use of the word 'deposit' on the call was the pad deposit.
Email handoff named but not explained — no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections.'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no hours or callback info.
Drive time between the house and the storage unit never priced into the estimate, despite two 10x20 units likely meaning multiple round trips.

Customer flagged a 'long' and somewhat steep walkway down to a circle drive — the exact path the pianos came in through — and Frank answered 'Okay. Okay.' and moved on without folding walk distance into the time estimate.
No moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
No zip codes captured; origin home size never established; additional stops never asked about.
top_strength: Frank's best move was mining the customer's own history instead of guessing. He tracked down her prior profile across two email addresses, found the September 22-24 three-day move, and then used the actual invoice to answer questions she couldn't — 'it looks like it was just around 75 boxes last time that we packed ourselves' and 'your final day was four and a half hours.' He also asked a genuinely good access question unprompted: 'is there any like access that might slow us down like, incline declined driveway, low hanging trees, narrow doorways.' The pad-deposit and buy-back explanation was a real proactive value-add most reps skip.
coaching_note: Frank, the single highest-leverage fix is that you never asked for the business. You confirmed Sept 11 was open in the first sixty seconds and then let a warm repeat customer hang up saying 'I need compare quotes now.' Before that email pitch, the line is: 'Sharron, we've got the eleventh open and there's no deposit to hold it — want me to lock that in for you now? If anything changes you can move it, you're not committed to a dollar.' Second priority: you gave her a rate and a bracket but never gave her a reason to pick us. Two pianos going into storage and she never heard No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000, never heard Meet Your Mover, never heard the On-Time Guarantee, and never heard what the $100/hour actually includes — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools. Right now her comparison shopping is pure price, because price is all you gave her. Third, and this is money straight back in her pocket: she told you 'I'm hoping to get all of the boxes done but we'll see' — that is your cue for both the packing quote and the Save Your Ass speech. 'Every box you finish before we show up is time off a $400-an-hour clock — consolidate the loose stuff, take a carload of the small items yourself, and you'll see it on the bill.' Last thing, and it's a small one that costs you rapport: get her name in the first thirty seconds and use it. She had to ask you yours at the end, and you'd already moved her once.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient with a decent proactive explanation of the pad program, but transactional throughout — zero name use, no affirmations or empathy markers, several stretches of dead-air 'let's see' while he looked things up, and he let the returning-customer moment pass with a flat 'Oh, no kidding.'
